info.title: Listmonk Shambhala sending API
info.summary: Send a center's e-mail from another system.
info.description:
For other systems (a member database, a booking system, a website) that send e-mail through a center: transactional e-mails and campaigns, from the center's templates. Each center has its own API, at its own address, and its own keys, made on its Config -> API page. The API doesn't subscribe people to the center's lists: sign-up webhooks do (`<center>/signup/openapi.json`).

Each key can do only what it was allowed to: send transactional e-mails (`messages`), send campaigns (`campaigns`), and/or read the events about the addresses it has sent to (`events`). Each operation that needs one says so in `x-denma-can`; anything else is refused with a 403. `GET /` says what a key can do, and when it expires, if it does.

Requests and answers are JSON. A successful answer is `{"data": ...}`; an error is `{"message": "..."}` with its status. Unknown fields in a request are refused, so a typo isn't silently ignored. A request is at most 16 MB, and a key makes at most 600 requests a minute. An address that sends 20 keys that don't work in 15 minutes is refused for a while.

E-mail is sent from the key's sender (set with the key: the center's, or another address at its sending domains), at most the key's daily limit of e-mails in 24 hours, under the center's daily cap, and never to anyone who complained, bounced, or whose domain can't receive mail; campaigns also skip whoever unsubscribed. A key also gives at most as many addresses (to send to, or a campaign's recipients: each counts, whether the center has it or not) and makes at most as many campaigns, drafts included, in 24 hours, before anyone's added (429). Answers say who wasn't sent to, but not why: a key's events say it, for the addresses it sends to. The center's sending through the API pauses on its own if its hard bounces reach 5% or its complaints 0.1% (Amazon SES's review levels); a superadmin resumes it.

Links in what a request sends (its subject, a campaign's body, `data`, recipients' `attribs`, images included) can go only to the key's link domains, set with the key, and the center's own (its sending domains, and this API's host); a request with a link elsewhere is refused (400), so that a leaked key can't send the center's e-mails with someone else's links. Links are found however they're written (HTML entities, backslashes, any attribute, CSS `url()`), and checked again as each e-mail is made, as the template's logic can make them: a transactional e-mail is then refused, and a campaign's e-mail isn't sent (a failed send). The center's template's own links are fine. A name can't have a link in it.

Consent: a campaign through the API goes to the addresses the other system gives, and the center has no record of their consent to it, so the other system has to have it (under Canada's anti-spam law, CASL, and others). The people it sends to are added to the center without lists and with no consent to the center's own mail: they can join its lists only by signing up themselves. Someone who unsubscribes from an API campaign unsubscribes from the whole center, and campaigns skip them from then on: send what people need whether or not they get newsletters (a booking's details, a password reset) as transactional e-mails (`POST /messages`), which still reach them.

Changes: since October 2026, `POST /subscribers` is gone (410): sign-up webhooks replace it. Keys have link domains, the notifications (the `events` webhook) tell a key that sends campaigns how they go (`campaign_*` events, with no `email`), and a campaign's new recipients keep its `attribs` (written once).

servers.description: A center's API. The copy of this document served by a center (`GET /openapi.json`) has that center's address here.

center.description: The center's address name, as in its public pages' address.

tags.name: Key
tags.description: The key and the center's templates.

tags.name: Campaigns
tags.description: A campaign to the addresses given, without adding them to the center's lists.

tags.name: Events
tags.description: Unsubscribes, complaints, bounces and blocklistings of the addresses the key has sent to, so that the other system can stop e-mailing them too; and how its campaigns go.

get.description: Which center and key this is, what the key can do, and how the center's sending stands.
This OpenAPI document, with the center's own address in `servers`. Needs no key.

The center's templates the API can name. They're made in the center, under Campaigns -> Templates, each with a name of its own: transactional templates (`tx`) for `POST /messages`, campaign and visual campaign templates for `POST /campaigns`.

200.description: The templates, transactional first, by name.

post.description:
A password reset, receipt or notice, to an address or up to 50, from a transactional template, from the key's sender. The template uses `{{ .Tx.Data.<name> }}` for `data`, and `{{ .Subscriber.Name }}`.

It goes to people who unsubscribed too, as it's not marketing; not to those who complained, bounced, or whose domain can't receive mail (`skipped`, "not sent"). Each new address is added to the center as a subscriber without lists, so that its bounces and complaints are recorded, with no consent to the center's own mail.

Its links (in `data` and `subject`, such as a password reset link) can go only to the key's link domains and the center's own.

All of it fits under the key's daily limit and the center's daily cap, or none of it is sent (429).

200.description: Who it was sent to, and who wasn't. The same `Idempotency-Key` again gets this answer, and sends nothing.

post.description:
A campaign to the `recipients` given (up to 10,000 a request), from a campaign or visual template, from the key's sender. The recipients go on a list of the campaign's own, not the center's lists, which is deleted a week after the campaign is done. Each recipient's `attribs` are used in the campaign's e-mails as `{{ .Subscriber.Attribs.<name> }}` (over the subscriber's own). A new address is added to the center with its name and `attribs`, written once, and with no consent to the center's own mail; a subscriber the center has keeps their record, and their name unless it's a stand-in (their address), which the name given replaces when the campaign starts. Attributes the center keeps itself (`consent_at`, `consent_source`, `consent_confirmed_at`, `consents`, `resubscribed_at`, `imported_at`, `tags`, and any starting `auto_blocklist_` or `denma_`) are refused. The campaign's `data` is `{{ .Campaign.Attribs.data.<name> }}`. With a campaign template, `body` (HTML) fills its `{{ template "content" . }}`. The e-mail has to have the center's footer: an unsubscribe link (`{{ UnsubscribeURL }}`), a view-in-browser link (`{{ MessageURL }}`), and the center's postal address, website and contact e-mail, which every campaign must show (Canada's anti-spam law, CASL, requires the address, a way to get in touch and the unsubscribe link). `{{ CenterFooter }}` gives both links (the center's templates have them all). One that doesn't, or whose images from the center's Media have since been deleted, doesn't start, and its `error` says why.

Its links (subject, `body`, `data`, `attribs`) can go only to the key's link domains and the center's own.

It starts once its addresses are checked, within seconds (`"status": "starting"`), or at `send_at`, and appears on the center's Campaigns page tagged `api`. If the center has set sending hours (Config → General), its e-mails go only within them: started outside them, it waits, and goes on when they open. Its recipients count against the key's daily limit when it starts (429 if they don't fit). Those who unsubscribed, complained or bounced are skipped, and listed in `skipped` ("not sent") once it's started: with `"start": false`, in the answer of `POST /campaigns/{id}/start`. How it goes (started, paused, resumed, finished, cancelled) is sent to the key's notifications address, if it has one.

For more than 10,000 recipients, make it with `"start": false`, add the rest with `POST /campaigns/{id}/recipients`, then `POST /campaigns/{id}/start`. One not started within 7 days is cancelled.

200.description: The campaign. The same `Idempotency-Key` again gets the campaign it made, and makes nothing.

400.description: The request isn't valid, or (when starting) no one can be sent the campaign: every recipient was skipped. Nothing was made.

get.description: One of the key's campaigns: its status, and how many were sent it, failed, opened, clicked and bounced.

post.description: Adds up to 10,000 recipients to a campaign made with `"start": false`, before it's started.

200.description: The campaign, with who wasn't added (`skipped`: not a valid address, attributes too big). Who won't be sent it is said when it starts.

post.description: Starts a campaign made with `"start": false`: within seconds, or at its `send_at`, its e-mails going within the center's sending hours if it has set them. Its recipients count against the key's daily limit (429 if they don't fit).

200.description: The campaign, starting, with who won't be sent it (`skipped`).

post.description: Cancels a campaign before it starts, while it's scheduled, or while it's sending.

get.description: The last 30 days' events about the addresses the key has sent to, from when it first did, oldest first: who unsubscribed, complained (marked an e-mail as spam), bounced (the address doesn't exist), or was blocklisted for another reason (its domain takes no mail, or it bounced from another center). The same events are sent to the key's webhook (`events`, under webhooks); this is for a system that can't take webhooks, or missed some. Ask again with `after` set to the answer's `after` while `more` is true.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Only events after this ID; 0 (or none) for the oldest kept.

post.summary: Unsubscribes, complaints, bounces, and how its campaigns go, as they happen
post.description:
The key's notifications, sent within a minute to its notifications address (set on Config -> API, `https://` only), in order, at most 100 events a request: with the `events` permission, its events (`GET /events`); if it sends campaigns, how each of its campaigns goes (`campaign_started`, `campaign_paused`, `campaign_resumed`, `campaign_finished`, `campaign_cancelled`, with `campaign_id` and no `email`; `GET /campaigns/{id}` has its figures). Answer with a 2xx; anything else is tried again later, waiting longer each time (up to 6 hours), and later events wait their turn. The Config -> API page can send a test event (`"type": "test"`).

Check the signature before trusting the request: `X-Listmonk-Signature` is `t=<unix time>,v1=<signature>`, the signature being the hex HMAC-SHA256, with the webhook's signing secret, of the time, a full stop and the request's body (`<t>.<body>`). Compare it in constant time, and refuse a request whose `t` is more than 5 minutes from your clock, so that a request someone captured can't be sent again later.

parameters.name: X-Listmonk-Signature
parameters.description: `t=<unix time>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<body>">`, with the webhook's signing secret.

default.description: Not taken: these events are sent again later.

apiKey.description: The key, made on the center's Config -> API page and shown once: `Authorization: Bearer lmk_...`. It can be limited to requests from some addresses, and can expire. When it's replaced, the old key can keep working for a while (up to a week), for the system using it to change over.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Any text up to 200 characters, unique to this send. The same key again (from the same API key) gets the first request's answer and sends nothing more, so a retry after a timeout never sends twice.

BadRequest.description: The request isn't valid; the message says why.

Unauthorized.description: No key, a key that isn't in use (any more), or one that has expired.

Forbidden.description: The key can't do this (`x-denma-can`), can't add people to a list asked for, or can't be used from this address.

NotFound.description: The key has no campaign with that ID.

Conflict.description: A request with this `Idempotency-Key` is still being handled, or the campaign isn't in a state for this (started, cancelled).

TooManyRequests.description: Over 600 requests a minute for this key; too many keys that don't work from this address; or the key's daily limit or the center's daily cap leaves no room for these e-mails, addresses or campaigns. The message says when to try again.

Paused.description: The center's sending through the API is paused (its bounce or complaint rate); a superadmin resumes it.

message.description: What's wrong, for a person to read.

Can.description: Something a key can do: send transactional e-mails, send campaigns (and be told how they go), read the events about the addresses it has sent to.

expires_at.description: When the key stops working, if it does.

sender.description: A sending key's: who its e-mails are from.

daily_limit.description: The most e-mails the key sends in 24 hours.

sent_24h.description: E-mails it sent (or started campaigns to) in the last 24 hours.

left.description: How many more it can send now.

daily_cap.description: The center's daily cap; 0 for none.

sent_24h.description: E-mails the center sent in the last 24 hours.

left.description: How many more it can send now; -1 without a cap.

paused.description: Whether the center's sending through the API is paused.

name.description: The name a request gives as `template`.

Skip.description: An address that wasn't sent to (or added). Why isn't said, unless it's the request's fault: the key's events say why, for the addresses it sends to.

to.description: An address, or a list of up to 50.

first_name.description: The recipient's first name, for a new address (at most 100 characters are kept); either it or `last_name` can be left out.

last_name.description: The recipient's last name, for a new address (at most 100 characters are kept).

name.description: The recipient's whole name, for a new address, without `first_name` and `last_name`: split at the first space (at most 200 characters are kept).

data.description: For the template: `{{ .Tx.Data.<name> }}`. Its links can go only to the key's link domains and the center's own.

reply_to.description: The Reply-To address, at one of the center's sending domains; else the center's, if it has one. (The sender is the key's.)

sent.description: The addresses it was sent to.

first_name.description: At most 100 characters are kept; either it or `last_name` can be left out. Kept by a new address, and by one whose name is a stand-in (their address) once the campaign starts.

name.description: Their whole name, without `first_name` and `last_name`: split at the first space. At most 200 characters are kept.

attribs.description: For the template, in this campaign's e-mails: `{{ .Subscriber.Attribs.<name> }}`, over the subscriber's own. A new address keeps them (written once); an existing subscriber's aren't changed. Up to 10,000 bytes; none the center keeps itself (`tags`, `consent_at`...).

template.description: A campaign or visual campaign template's name (`GET /templates`).

subject.description: The subject; it can use template tags.

name.description: The campaign's name on the Campaigns page; else its subject.

body.description: HTML filling a campaign template's `{{ template "content" . }}`. Not with a visual template, which is the whole e-mail.

reply_to.description: The Reply-To address, at one of the center's sending domains; else the center's, if it has one. (The sender is the key's.)

tags.description: Tags for the campaign on the Campaigns page (it's always tagged `api`).

send_at.description: When to send it, in the future; else now.

start.description: `false` to make it without starting it, to add recipients first.

recipients.description: Who it goes to. Needed unless `"start": false`.

status.description: `draft`: made with `"start": false`; `starting`: its addresses being checked; then `scheduled` or `running`, and `finished` or `cancelled`. `paused` when the center's sending is paused.

error.description: Why it didn't start, if it didn't.

recipients.description: How many addresses it has, while it's a draft; once started, how many can be sent it (the others are in `skipped`).

skipped.description: Who wasn't added (not a valid address, attributes too big), and, once it's started (as it's made, or by `POST /campaigns/{id}/start`), who won't be sent it ("not sent").

id.description: Its place in the feed, increasing: events come in this order, each after those already given, so `after` never skips one. `GET /events?after=` takes it.

type.description: `unsubscribed`; `complained` (marked an e-mail as spam); `bounced` (a hard bounce: the address doesn't exist); `blocklisted` for another reason (its domain takes no mail, or it bounced from another center); `campaign_*`: one of the key's campaigns started, paused, resumed, finished or was cancelled (to a key that sends campaigns); `test`, from the Config -> API page, to webhooks only.

email.description: The address it's about; none for a campaign's.

campaign_id.description: The campaign it came from, if known.

after.description: The last event's ID: `after` for the next page.
